_comment: Per-family ledger for the content-defect SEO families aggregated by follow-up issues #5845 and #6222. One entry per family: which gate MEASURES it, what its ceiling is, and the run the ceiling was sealed from. Read scripts/lib/seoDefectRatchet.mjs for the semantics and for why a ceiling is not a threshold relaxation here (AGENTS.md non-negotiable #1's delimited reassembled-corpus exception, owner 2026-08-20). `ceilingRatePct` is offenders per 100 files SCANNED — a rate, because post-deploy-validate-dist.yml pins AUDIT_SAMPLE_RATE=0.25 and a sampled count is not comparable to a full walk. Ceilings only DESCEND: scripts/lib/seoDefectRatchet.mjs::tightenLedger throws on a raise, and tests/seo/seo-defect-ratchet.test.ts asserts that it does.

_enforcement.ratchet: the auditor reads this entry and fails only above the ceiling. Used ONLY where the pre-existing verdict was zero tolerance over a corpus with a large historical population, i.e. permanently red.
_enforcement.zero-tolerance: the auditor keeps its own hard 0 and does NOT read this file. The entry exists so the family is tracked and so a regression from 0 is attributable to a named issue bullet. Zero is already the tightest ceiling reachable — putting a ratchet here would be a relaxation.
_enforcement.existing-baseline: the family already had a rate ratchet before this ledger, in its own baseline file. Recorded here for traceability; the ceiling lives in the file named by `baselineFile`.
_enforcement.unmeasured: no corpus-wide automatic measure exists at a granularity this ledger can ratchet. No ceiling is invented. `blocker` says what would unblock it.

_measurementSource.note: AUDIT_SAMPLE_RATE=0.25 walks a rotating quarter of dist/ per run; four consecutive runs cover the corpus. Every ceiling below was sealed from the WORST (highest) of the four buckets listed in `buckets`, so the ratchet starts green on any of them rather than on the lucky one.

single-h1-per-page.issue: #5845 item 1 — 12 job pages with multiple H1 (embedded ATS markup)

measurement.note: 0 offenders on all four buckets, i.e. 0 across the whole ~4.03M-file dist/. The 12 pages the issue cites no longer exist in the corpus; the bullet is closable on this measurement.

link-anchor-text-non-descriptive.issue: #5845 item 2 — 48 non-descriptive anchors; also the anchor half of #6222 item 1
link-anchor-text-non-descriptive.status: red before this ledger — the auditor's `nonDescriptiveTotal === 0` clause is a hard zero next to a carefully-built rate gate for its own sibling half (`unnamedAnchors`, which passes)

measurement.note: Sealed from the worst bucket. THE NOISE FLOOR IS WIDE AND THAT IS NOT HIDDEN: at ~12 offenders per draw the Poisson sigma is ~3.5, so `minAbsDelta: 12` (~3 sigma) means the gate fires around 30 in a bucket, i.e. it catches a doubling of the population and not a drift of five. That is the honest limit of ratcheting a small count on a 25 % sample. The real close for this family is not a tighter ceiling: all offenders are enumerated in the failure message and in dist/audit-reports/link-anchor-text.json, and they are two templates — `/cerca-lavoro-ticino/ricerca/page-N/` pagination ('scopri'/'continua'/'mehr') plus one article using 'qui'.

cluster-canonical-hreflang.blocker: No corpus-wide automatic measure exists at ratchet granularity. The 347 came from a measurement that the gate's own header now records as ~100 % false positive (the regexes required `rel="canonical"` where the build's minifier emits `rel=canonical`; 146 canonical and 199-of-199 hreflang offenders on run 31891126686 were all artifacts). What replaced it, in #6216, is a fixed SYSTEMIC_RATE_CEILING over a stride sample of 50 cluster pages per locale — n=200. A ceiling ratchet on n=200 at a ~1 % rate has a binomial sigma near the signal itself and would flap on which stride the sample took, which is the failure mode that gets a gate switched off. Inventing a threshold here would be a fake ratchet, so none is written.
cluster-canonical-hreflang.corroboration: The two canonical/hreflang gates that DO walk the corpus were green on the same run 32826787615: audit:hreflang 0 offenders, audit:canonical-trailing-slash 1 (passing). That is independent evidence the 347 was the measurement bug and not a population — but neither gate is scoped to cluster pages, so neither can close this bullet on its own.
cluster-canonical-hreflang.unblockedBy: a cluster-scoped canonical/hreflang auditor folded into audit:all's single walk. scripts/audit-hreflang.mjs and scripts/audit-canonical-trailing-slash.mjs already walk dist/ corpus-wide, but as separate Node processes outside the unified runner and without the cluster-page scoping this family needs, so their counts are not on this ledger's scale. Folding them in is the same migration #5845 item 6 performed for the four auditors above.

measurement.note: Passing, with baselineDelta.regression = 0. The per-feature rate ratchet in data/title-length-baseline.json already does what this ledger would do; duplicating the ceiling here would create two sources of truth for one family.
0 offenders on all four buckets. The 53 pages the issue cites are gone; the bullet is closable on this measurement.

duplicate-meta-description.issue: #6222 item 1 — duplicate meta descriptions stay red on the same run
duplicate-meta-description.status: red before this ledger — zero tolerance over ~197'000 historical offender pages

measurement.note: The offender unit is a DESCRIPTION GROUP over 2 pages, not a page. Bucket-to-bucket the rate moves only 4.8815..4.9042 %, so unlike the anchor family this one ratchets tightly: relPct 0 with absPp 0.10 caps at 5.0043 %, ~3 sigma on n=49k. Concentrated, not diffuse: the top group alone is 11'179 pages sharing one expired-job boilerplate ('This position has been updated or removed' and its three locale twins), so a single template fix moves the rate by a visible amount and the ceiling descends with it.

duplicate-structured-data.issue: not named in #5845/#6222 — sibling auditor folded in by #5845 item 6, tracked so the fold's four auditors are all accounted for
